key_decisions.rationale: Preserves foreknowledge, the Elijah setting, and his appeal against Israel.
key_decisions.before: God has not rejected his people whom he foreknew. Or do you not know what Scripture says in the story of Elijah, how he appeals to God against Israel?
key_decisions.after: God has not rejected his people whom he foreknew. Or do you not know what Scripture says in the passage about Elijah, how he appeals to God against Israel?
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: God has not rejected his people whom he foreknew. Or do you not know what the Scripture says in Elijah, how he pleads with God against Israel?

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps God's self-reservation, the exact number, specific men, and Baal's name.
key_decisions.before: But what does the divine answer say to him? “I have kept for myself seven thousand who have not bowed the knee to Baal.”
key_decisions.after: But what does the divine response say to him? “I have kept for myself seven thousand men who have not bowed the knee to Baal.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: But what does the divine response say to him? “I have left for myself seven thousand men who have not bowed the knee to Baal.”

key_decisions.rationale: Maintains corporate Israel, the chosen group, and hardening without hiding the passive.
key_decisions.before: What then? Israel did not obtain what it was seeking, but the chosen obtained it. The rest were hardened,
key_decisions.after: What then? Israel did not obtain what it was seeking, but the chosen remnant obtained it. The rest were hardened,
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: What then? Israel did not obtain what it seeks, but the elect obtained it, and the rest were hardened,

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps the denial, trespass, Gentile salvation, and stated provocative purpose.
key_decisions.before: I ask, then: Did they stumble so that they would fall beyond recovery? Absolutely not! Rather, through their trespass salvation has come to the Gentiles, to make Israel jealous.
key_decisions.after: So I ask: Did they stumble in order to fall beyond recovery? Absolutely not! Rather, through their trespass salvation has come to the Gentiles, to make Israel jealous.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: I say then, did they stumble so that they might fall? May it never be! But by their transgression salvation has come to the Gentiles, to provoke them to jealousy.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves the lesser-to-greater argument and the unresolved fullness term.
key_decisions.before: Now if their trespass means riches for the world, and their loss means riches for the Gentiles, how much more will their fullness mean!
key_decisions.after: Now if their trespass means riches for the world, and their loss means riches for the Gentiles, how much more will their fullness mean?
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: Now if their transgression is riches for the world and their failure riches for the Gentiles, how much more their fullness!

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves horticultural detail and Gentile participation without replacement language.
key_decisions.before: But if some of the branches were broken off, and you, though a wild olive shoot, were grafted in among them and became a sharer in the rich root of the olive tree,
key_decisions.after: But if some of the branches were broken off, and you, though a wild olive shoot, were grafted in among them and became a sharer in the rich root of the olive tree,
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: But if some of the branches were broken off, and you, being a wild olive shoot, were grafted in among them and became a fellow-partaker of the root of the rich olive tree,

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps both causes and the command to fear rather than boast.
key_decisions.before: True. They were broken off because of lack of trust, and you stand through trust. Do not become arrogant, but fear.
key_decisions.after: True enough. They were broken off because of unbelief, but you stand by faith. Do not become arrogant; instead, be afraid.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: True; they were broken off because of unbelief, but you stand by faith. Do not be arrogant, but fear;

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves kindness, severity, condition, and threat of being cut off.
key_decisions.before: Consider, then, God’s kindness and severity: severity toward those who fell, but God’s kindness toward you, if you continue in his kindness. Otherwise you too will be cut off.
key_decisions.after: Consider, then, God's kindness and severity: severity toward those who fell, but God's kindness toward you, if you remain in his kindness. Otherwise, you too will be cut off.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: Behold then the kindness and severity of God: toward those who have fallen, severity; but toward you, kindness, if you continue in that kindness; otherwise you also will be cut off.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves mystery, partial hardening, Israel, temporal limit, and Gentile fullness.
key_decisions.before: I do not want you to be unaware of this mystery, brothers and sisters, so that you do not become wise in your own eyes: a partial hardening has come upon Israel until the fullness of the Gentiles comes in,
key_decisions.after: For I do not want you to be unaware of this mystery, brothers and sisters, so that you will not be wise in your own estimation: a partial hardening has come upon Israel until the fullness of the Gentiles comes in,
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: For I do not want you to be unaware of this mystery, brothers, lest you be wise in yourselves: that a partial hardening has come upon Israel until the fullness of the Gentiles has come in,

key_decisions.rationale: Uses in this way for houtōs and preserves all Israel without defining it in the main text.
key_decisions.before: and in this way all Israel will be saved, just as it is written, “The Deliverer will come from Zion; he will turn ungodliness away from Jacob.
key_decisions.after: and in this way all Israel will be saved, as it is written: “The Deliverer will come from Zion; he will turn godlessness away from Jacob.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: and so all Israel will be saved, just as it is written, “The Deliverer will come from Zion, he will remove ungodliness from Jacob;

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves the paired perspectives without turning enemies into a timeless ethnic label.
key_decisions.before: With respect to the good news, they are enemies for your sake; but with respect to election, they are beloved because of the ancestors.
key_decisions.after: With respect to the good news, they are enemies for your sake; but with respect to election, they are beloved because of the patriarchs.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: According to the gospel they are enemies for your sake, but according to election they are beloved for the sake of the fathers;

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps the parallel, repeated now, and mercy as the intended outcome.
key_decisions.before: so they too have now disobeyed so that, through the mercy shown to you, they too may now receive mercy.
key_decisions.after: so they too have now disobeyed because of the mercy shown to you, so that they too may now receive mercy.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: so also these now have been disobedient, so that by the mercy shown to you they also may now receive mercy.

key_decisions.rationale: Retains universal confinement and universal mercy within Paul's sentence.
key_decisions.before: For God has enclosed everyone in disobedience so that he may show mercy to everyone.
key_decisions.after: For God has confined everyone under disobedience so that he may have mercy on everyone.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: For God has shut up all into disobedience so that he may show mercy to all.
